answer.rationale: Rollback (memory_b1) is off the table: compliance has ruled the security patch non-revertible, so the one prior success most similar to this symptom pattern is unavailable. That leaves the write-path pressure to be relieved indirectly. memory_b5 is the only inherited record that speaks directly to relieving primary write latency, so it is the first verification target — but its stated mechanism was offloading dashboard/report reads, and I do not know that the current climb has the same cause. The timing correlation with a release 2 hours ago suggests the new build itself may be the driver, in which case shedding read load is palliative and buys time rather than fixing anything. I want the original record to see whether the day-55 event involved a write-path regression or purely read contention. memory_b2 is the second target because regional failover is the tempting high-leverage move and the consolidated summary is suspiciously clean ('traffic shifted cleanly'); before shifting regions during peak settlement with heavy writes I need to know from the source whether that March event was write-heavy and whether in-flight writes were confirmed durable, since the primary objective forbids losing customer writes. I am deliberately not choosing failover on the strength of a summary. add_capacity (memory_b3) worked when provisioned ahead of a known peak, not 90 minutes into an active degradation, so it likely lands too late. enable_circuit_breaker (memory_b4) contained a failing external dependency; nothing here indicates a partner fault, and failing fast on our own write path would drop the very writes I am charged with preserving. So I intend read-replica routing, held to a small guarded slice — a subset of report/analytical queries with the write-path p99 watched as the readout — because it is reversible in seconds and reveals whether read contention is actually a meaningful share of the load. Downstream value risk: replicas serve stale data, and if any settlement or reconciliation logic reads through the paths I move, stale reads could produce incorrect financial state, which is worse than latency; I would exclude settlement-critical reads from the routed slice. If the guarded slice does not move p99, that is evidence the release is the cause and the next window should go to a forward fix rather than another traffic-shaping attempt.
